Hatherley keeps his story but loses his thumb. Holmes points out the consolation: Hatherley now has, at the very least, a story to dine out on for life. "You have lost a thumb, but you have gained a reputation," Holmes says.

The case, dated to the summer of 1889, was one of those whose villain Holmes never brought to justice — but whose puzzle he solved completely within twenty-four hours.

sample_payloads.title: The Adventure of the Engineer's Thumb
sample_payloads.text: The patient introduced himself as Victor Hatherley, a hydraulic engineer of twenty-six. He had set up his own consulting practice the year before at 16A Victoria Street, with capital inherited on coming of age. Business had been quiet: only three consultations and one small commission in the year. Hatherley lived alone, took meals at a restaurant, and had no near relatives in London.
